correctness.rationale: All labelled k-point graph patterns are independent binary edge coordinates by Rado universality. Seidel-cut translations have rank k-1 for k>=1; complement adds one generator exactly when k>=3, since all cuts have even triangle parity. Restriction to n named old vertices is surjective on the finite translation subspace, so each fibre has exactly 2^{Delta-d(k)+d(n)} orbits. The full symmetric group yields one. Omega-categoricity turns orbits into complete types, and complement/switch triangle parity show equality of pointwise stabilizers at n=2 and n=3. A separate brute-force quotient enumerator validates all 105 cases at n+r<=5 and 32 subgroup rank checks through k=7, without substituting finite checks for infinite proof. Risk: interpretation of local generator operations as exact reduct orbits relies on Thomas and Bodirsky–Pinsker classification and random graph extension property.

value.rationale: This gives a complete all-size parametric closed formula for a natural oligomorphic invariant of each of the five classical reducts. More substantively it identifies a sharp, counterintuitive failure of monotonicity under naming parameters: one named point lowers the minimal arity for distinguishing all five groups, while two named points make five-way numeric separation impossible at any arity, with an additional permanent pairwise collapse at three named points. The boundary is explained structurally by equality of pointwise stabilizers, so the result is more than a short finite table or a restatement of the reduct classification.
